name: SentinelOne
description: The SentinelOne fleet, read-only: the latest threats and console activity, exposure to a CVE, whether an indicator has been seen, which endpoints run an application, and the state of the agents.

operations.summary: The most recent threats detected in the fleet, newest first: what, on which host, and whether it was mitigated.
operations.ask_when: the question asks about the latest or recent threats, detections, alerts, incidents or events in SentinelOne, or what happened most recently.

operations.summary: The most recent entries in the SentinelOne activity log, newest first: agent, policy, user and threat events.
operations.ask_when: the question asks about the latest or recent activity, the activity log, or what changed or happened in the SentinelOne console lately.

operations.summary: Threats whose details mention a file, process, path or hash -- how many, and on how many endpoints.
operations.ask_when: the question names a file, process, path or hash and asks how many endpoints alerted for it, where it was detected, or whether it was seen as a threat.

text.description: the file name, process, path or hash, e.g. invoice_viewer.exe

response.summary: {count} threats matched, on {distinct:agentRealtimeInfo.agentComputerName} distinct endpoints (up to 300 threats are fetched).
response.empty: No threat in SentinelOne mentions that.

operations.summary: The threats SentinelOne recorded on a named endpoint (host / computer name): how many, newest first, and their state.
operations.ask_when: the question names an endpoint, host or computer and asks how many alerts, threats or detections it has, or what was detected on it.

host.description: the endpoint's computer name or part of it, e.g. WS-FINANCE-07

response.summary: {count} threats recorded on {distinct:agentRealtimeInfo.agentComputerName} endpoint(s) matching that name ({distinct:threatInfo.threatName} distinct threat names; up to 300 are fetched).
response.empty: SentinelOne has no threats recorded on an endpoint by that name.

operations.summary: Which endpoints in the fleet are exposed to a given CVE. Slow on a large fleet: it can take minutes and time out.
operations.ask_when: the question names a CVE id and asks who or what is exposed, affected, vulnerable or at risk in the fleet. It is slow and may time out: when NVD is also connected, look the CVE up there too, and check the inventory (app_inventory) for the affected product it names.

response.empty: No fleet endpoint is recorded as exposed to this CVE.

operations.summary: Whether an indicator of compromise has been seen in the tenant.
operations.ask_when: the question gives an indicator — a file hash, IP address, domain or URL — and asks whether it has been seen, is known, or is malicious.

indicator.description: a hash, IP, domain or URL to look up

response.empty: This indicator is not in the tenant's threat-intelligence records.

operations.summary: Which applications in the fleet match a name, and on how many endpoints each is installed.
operations.ask_when: the question asks whether a named application is installed, present or in use in the fleet, on how many endpoints, or which hosts have it -- this needs only the application's name, and it is the lookup to use when the vendor isn't given.

response.empty: No such application is in the fleet inventory.
response.summary: {count} applications match. The most widely installed of them is on {max:endpointsCount} endpoints, so at least that many endpoints have one. Installs across all of them add up to {sum:endpointsCount}, but helpers, updaters and variants sit on the same machines, so that is not a count of endpoints.

operations.summary: Which endpoints run an application, and at what version.
operations.ask_when: the question asks where a named application is installed, on which hosts, or what versions of it are running.

vendor.description: the application's vendor exactly as the inventory lists it, e.g. Zoom Communications, Inc.

response.empty: No endpoint is recorded as running that application.

operations.summary: The agents in the fleet: how many, and their state.
operations.ask_when: the question asks how many agents or endpoints there are, the size of the fleet, or the state of a named host's agent.

host.description: optional: a computer name to narrow to

operations.summary: How many agents report an OS version containing the given text (e.g. 15.8.1, 26.7.1), counted by SentinelOne.
operations.ask_when: the question asks how many endpoints, devices or agents run a given OS version or release (macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, Windows 11 23H2, Ubuntu 22.04).

version.description: the version number or text the OS version contains, e.g. 15.8.1 -- one version per call

response.line: {totalItems} agents report an OS version containing that.
response.empty: No agent reports that OS version.

operations.summary: When the application inventory and vulnerability scan runs: how often, on which days, at what time, and whether extensive and vulnerability scanning are on.
operations.ask_when: the question asks when the application inventory or vulnerability scan runs, ran last, or runs next, or how it is scheduled.

response.line: Inventory scan: every {scanSchedule.scanEvery|default:?} on {scanSchedule.repeatOn|join|default:(no days set)} at {scanSchedule.time|default:?} ({scanSchedule.timezone|default:timezone not set}); extensive scan {extensiveScanEnabled}; vulnerability scanning {vulnerabilitiesScanEnabled}. SentinelOne reports the schedule, not a timestamp of the last run: the last and next runs follow from it.
